Last thing (hopefully) on this topic -- after I've extracted the information using percMethylation and adjusted the data outside of methylKit ...is there a function within the package to then put this to coerce the matrix back into a methylBase object? 

(Basically I want to replace the original methylation values with my corrected values...but keep the treatment/sample/etc. information all the same)

Looking at the code I'm sure I can figure out a way to accomplish this, but I figured it wouldn't hurt to ask in case it already exists and I'm just missing it?

Unfortunately, there is no function for that. But, writing one should be straightforward.

You need to get the data part of the methylBase object with getData(), assume "x" is the methylBase object and "mat" is the adjusted percent methylation matrix which is originally obtained from "x"
dat=getData(x)


Then, you need to adjust C and T counts on the data, the code below assumes the column and row order of the CpGs doesn't change between the methylation matrix "mat" and the data frame part of methylBase object "dat"

dat[,x@numCs.index]=round(dat[,x@coverage.index]*mat/100)
dat[,x@numTs.index]=dat[,x@coverage.index] -  dat[,x@numCs.index]



Lastly, create a new methylBase obj, overwriting the old one:
 x=new("methylBase",dat,sample.ids=x@sample.ids,
                             assembly=x@assembly,context=x@context,
                             treatment=x@treatment,coverage.index=x@coverage.index,
                             numCs.index=x@numCs.index,numTs.index=x@numTs.index,
                             destranded=x@destranded,resolution=x@resolution )

I haven't tested this code, but something along these lines should work.

Best
Altuna Akalin

Hi Shannon,
Here is a temporary fix to memory allocation problem for large number of files, I updated the objects format and made unite() function faster. Here is how you can run this for methylKit version 0.5.7.

library(methylKit)

source("http://gist.github.com/al2na/ba70ab6d3911830e0fca/raw/98f5f498f2e323be968def16991720d349139de9/updateObjects.R")
source("http://gist.github.com/al2na/a9ea925fc11af26b9c72/raw/597d962cf221e14e60fef09d25aff007f833264a/newUnite.R")


# here is an example of how it works:
data(methylKit) # get example data

# you need to update methylKit objects to the new format
# this function works on all methylKit objects
new.obj=updateObject(methylRawList.obj) # ignore messages or warnings

object.size(new.obj)
object.size(methylRawList.obj)

# the new unit function that works on new methylRawList
unite2(new.obj)

Let me know if this works or not, or if it improves performance at all. The new objects are almost 2-3 times smaller than old ones.

EDIT: This feature has been added to latest version v0.9.1

Best,
Altuna
